newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares unperturbed by economic data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares unperturbed by economic data.

text.p: The Singapore stock market eased marginally on light profit-taking on Tuesday morning but dealers were unmoved by the government's latest economic data.

"We saw some profit-taking this morning but it was not significant. There was no bad news in the economic data released this morning. All the figures were as announced previously and therefore discounted," said a dealer with a local house.
The Ministry of Trade and Industry maintained its economic growth projection for Singapore at 5.0 to 7.0 percent in 1997.
At 0215 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index had shed 7.84 points to 2,28.26. Turnover was around 116 million shares, with losers outpacing gainers by 217 to 99.
Fruit and vegetable supplier FHTK led the actives, with over 5.4 million shares, which were down Singapore $0.005 (US$0.004) at S$0.70.
Speculative Malaysian counters like Berjaya Industries stayed active on keen retail interest and rotational play, dealers said.

There was a surge in activity in Malaysia's Chocolate Products. "The stock has been out of action when the Malaysian counters were very active. It was one of the laggards and now it's getting played," said another dealer.
